name: Rape and sex-offender registries worldwide

88df150450a75c23.h:
Zimbabwe

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: Still none, by a newer source. Pan African Visions (8 July 2026): the Justice Ministry has only begun consultations, with UNICEF, on whether to set up a sex offenders register and how it would fit privacy and rehabilitation rules. SMART/Library of Congress, 'SORN Laws around the World' (2022; info cutoff Oct 2021), Appendix 'Notable countries currently without sex offender registries', p. 197 (PDF p. 208). Status 'Under consideration': 2011 report of a register being set up and 2016 judicial proposal; no operating register.

d76e24e993b639ef.h:
Venezuela

No registry running, a source says: Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Impact / Together for Girls), indicator 2.3 'Background checks', Data_summary sheet of the official workbook: 'Venezuela's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children.' This states that no child-work vetting scheme or conviction-based bar exists in national law; it does not separately address a police-only offender register. Also read this pass: the Ley para la Prevención y Erradicación del Abuso Sexual contra Niñas, Niños y Adolescentes (Gaceta Oficial 6.655 Ext., 7 Oct 2021; text at https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-05/6-prevencionabusosexual_digital_v1.pdf). It sets up no register. Its only conviction consequence is loss of parental authority (art. 19). The 2021 reform of the Ley Orgánica sobre el Derecho de las Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia (Gaceta 6.667 Ext., 16 Dec 2021) creates only a 'registro único de denuncias', a register of complaints, not of offenders. CRC documents checked: CRC/C/VEN/CO/2, CO/3-5, CRC/C/OPSC/VEN/CO/1 (3 Nov 2014). No register mentioned.

Thailand

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: No newer information found (October 2026). No register law was found after the 2022 Act on preventive measures against repeat sexual or violent offences (post-release supervision, not a register). Journal of Social Science and Buddhistic Anthropology article 'The Appropriate Format of Sex Offenders' Registration in the Context of Thailand' (2022) states 'สำหรับประเทศไทยยังไม่มีการนำมาตรการขึ้นทะเบียนผู้กระทำความผิดทางเพศมาใช้แบบเป็นรูปธรรม' (Thailand has not yet concretely adopted sex offender registration) and recommends a new Act. The Preventive Measures Against Recidivism in Sexual or Violent Offences Act B.E. 2565 (Royal Gazette 25 Oct 2022) provides court-ordered post-release supervision, treatment and electronic monitoring for up to 10 years, but the news summary of it (https://thestandard.co/act-prevention-of-repeated-sexual-offenses/) mentions no register or public disclosure. Not in the 2022 SORN report or the SMART/ICMEC overview.

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: No newer information found (October 2026). No 2022-2026 register, vetting scheme or bill was found (English/Nepali search). ECPAT International Nepal Legal Checklist (November 2021): 'No' - 'Nepal does not have a sex offender registry mandated by law.' On background checks: 'Unable to find legal provisions that mandate background checks'; Children Act s. 67(1) dismisses a public or private employee who commits an offence against a child and makes them ineligible for up to ten years for work involving direct contact with children. English search 'Nepal sex offender registry child sexual abuse offenders database' and ECPAT Country Overview Nepal 2020 (https://www.ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/ECPAT-Country-Overview-Report-Nepal-2020.pdf, text search) found no register. No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: No newer information found (October 2026). No 2022-2026 register or bill was found (Portuguese search). Disrupting Harm em Moçambique (ECPAT, INTERPOL, UNICEF Innocenti; Portuguese edition 2022), PDF p. 24: government representatives said it is necessary to 'Criar um registo nacional de criminosos sexuais' (create a national register of sex offenders) [interview RA1-MZ-12-A]; recommendation 5.1 (p. 87) calls for case-monitoring systems 'incluindo registos de criminosos sexuais'. This implies no register existed at the time of the research (c. 2021). Portuguese search 'Moçambique registo de condenados por crimes sexuais contra menores agressores sexuais base de dados' found only statistics on sexual crimes (AIM, WLSA) and Portuguese (Portugal) register news. ECPAT 2011 A4A Mozambique report: no register mentioned. Not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016.

6370725d43d61ac3.h:
Mongolia

No registry running, a source says: Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Impact / Together for Girls), indicator 2.3 'Background checks', Data_summary sheet of the official workbook: 'Mongolia's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children.' This states that no child-work vetting scheme or conviction-based bar exists in national law; it does not separately address a police-only offender register. Other findings this pass: the 2016 Law on Child Protection (legalinfo.mn/mn/detail/11710), art. 18.1.8, told the central child-protection agency to 'build a database, together with law enforcement, on citizens and legal entities who committed crimes or violations against children, children in conflict with the law, and witness and victim children' and use it in its work. That law was replaced by the revised Law on Child Protection of 17 Jan 2024. The Ministry's final draft of the revision (mlsp.gov.mn/uploads/files/khuukhed_khamgaalal_law_draft_final_last.pdf) no longer has this perpetrator database. It keeps only a database of at-risk children and services (art. 2.3, item 2.10) and a bar on appointing persons convicted of crimes against children as guardians (art. 4.10.1.4). The enacted 2024 text could not be retrieved: legalinfo.mn search is script-driven. No implementation of the 2016 database was found. CRC documents checked: CRC/C/MNG/CO/3-4 and CO/5, CRC/C/OPSC/MNG/CO/1 (3 Mar 2010), state reports and lists of issues. None mentions a register.

294c9fea6bcbc5a4.h:
Moldova

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: A bill is pending. A Labour Code reform (Draft Law No. 218/2026) would bar people convicted of offences against children from jobs with regular contact with children and require a detailed criminal-record certificate that also shows expunged convictions. Parliament passed it in first reading on 2 July and, per Moldova's Council of Europe reply, in second reading on 30 July 2026, but it was not yet published, so not in force; it is a vetting rule, not a register. Ministry of Internal Affairs, 9 Oct 2024 ('Child protection measures and Moldova's presidency of the Council of Europe'): draft measures include 'the development of a system to register offenders convicted of sexual abuse', and officials discussed study visits and expertise sharing 'to develop the concept of a sex offenders registry' - i.e. none existed then. Ombudsman letter to the Ministry of Justice, 11 Apr 2022 (https://ombudsman.md/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/opinie-asigurarea-drepturilor-victimelor-in-cazul-infractiunilor-privind-viata-sexuala-si-violenta-in-familie.pdf) asked for 'examinarea posibilităţii/oportunităţii creării unui registru electronic de evidenţă a persoanelor condamnate pentru infracţiuni cu caracter sexual împotriva copiilor'. Moldova's reply to the Lanzarote Committee questionnaire on screening of professionals (received 31 Jul 2026, https://rm.coe.int/moldova-replies-to-the-thematic-questionnaire-screening-of-professiona/48802cd7b2, read via WebFetch) names no dedicated register: screening uses the general State Register of Criminalistic and Criminological Information (Ministry of Internal Affairs IT Service) and ordinary/detailed criminal-record certificates (Law 216/2003; MIA Order 306/2023); Labour Code Art. 296(2) bars persons deprived by a court of the right to teach, or with records for certain offences, from pedagogical work. A bill adding mandatory criminal-record and psychological checks for all jobs with regular contact with children passed first reading on 2 Jul 2026 (Moldpres, https://moldpres.md/eng/society/persons-convicted-of-offences-against-children-no-to-be-allowed-to-hold-positions-involving-interaction-with-minors) and was not in force as of 31 Jul 2026. Not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016.

No 2022-2026 register, vetting scheme or bill was found (French search); 2024 reforms added castration penalties, not a register. The Feb 2024 penal code reform allowing surgical/chemical castration of child rapists was checked in four news reports (allafrica 202402100139, le360, theafricanmirror, allafrica 202412310228 [403]); none mentions a register. Not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016.

f40c31aa32ac7dac.h:
Liechtenstein

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: Still none, by a newer source. Liechtenstein's Lanzarote reply (received 9 July 2026) says it 'does not maintain any other relevant registers, such as a specific registry for convicted sex offenders'. Screening relies on the general criminal-record extract, which the candidate must request (CHF 20). Strafregistergesetz (Gesetz über das Strafregister und die Tilgung gerichtlicher Verurteilungen), read via WebFetch: only a general criminal record certificate (Art. 8); no special certificate for work with minors and no sex offender register; Art. 11a doubles expungement periods for listed sexual offences. This is an inference from the statute text, not an explicit statement.

No registry running, a source says: The 2022 US survey covers this country in one sentence about the whole region (no country there had registry laws), not in its own entry. Re-checked October 2026: No newer information found (October 2026). No register, vetting scheme or bill was found (Arabic search). SORN Laws around the World (Library of Congress FRD for DOJ SMART, Apr 2022; research cutoff Oct 2021), section 4.4 'Near East (North Africa and Middle East)', printed p. 141 (PDF p. 152): '[Researchers determined that no countries within this region had laws pertaining to SORs.]' The appendix for the region (printed pp. 205-206) lists only Israel, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. This is a region-wide statement, not a country-specific one, and dates from Oct 2021. Also searched: WebSearch (ar) 'ليبيا سجل مرتكبي الجرائم الجنسية الاعتداء على الأطفال قاعدة بيانات' - nothing for Libya. Not in SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016.

866acfdf519dc61d.h:
Kosovo

No registry running, a source says: Telegrafi / Radio Evropa e Lirë, 31 Aug 2022: after a child rape case, NGO coalition KOMF called for 'krijimin e databazës së personave të dënuar për vepra penale kundër integritetit seksual të fëmijëve' (creation of a database of persons convicted of sexual offences against children); the article asks 'A mund të krijohet në Kosovë regjistri i dhunuesve seksualë?' and says, per authorities and justice experts, a public register is hard to set up under current law. The Government's draft Criminal Code amendment (Decision 02/100, 12 Oct 2022, https://kryeministri.rks-gov.net/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Projektligji-per-ndryshim-plotesimin-e-Kodit-Penale-te-Republikes-se-Kosoves.pdf, new Art. 66(7)) proposed that the Kosovo Judicial Council 'shall maintain and publish a register' of persons convicted of rape, sexual assault and domestic violence (also reported by Prishtina Insight, https://prishtinainsight.com/kosovo-moves-to-toughen-penalties-for-rape-domestic-violence/). The law as enacted, Law No. 08/L-188 (Official Gazette No. 23, 23 Nov 2023, https://md.rks-gov.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/D63E0C47-F3DF-42E2-B138-D23402018A92.pdf), contains no register clause and no mention of the Judicial Council (checked by text search of the English version); it adds bans on public-sector employment (Art. 62A) and on running for public office for rape convictions. No later law creating a register was found. Not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016.

No registry running, a source says: The 2022 US survey covers this country in one sentence about the whole region (no country there had registry laws), not in its own entry. Re-checked October 2026: No newer information found (October 2026). No register, vetting scheme or bill was found (Arabic search). SORN Laws around the World (Library of Congress FRD for DOJ SMART, Apr 2022; research cutoff Oct 2021), section 4.4 'Near East (North Africa and Middle East)', printed p. 141 (PDF p. 152): '[Researchers determined that no countries within this region had laws pertaining to SORs.]' The appendix for the region (printed pp. 205-206) lists only Israel, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. This is a region-wide statement, not a country-specific one, and dates from Oct 2021. No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: No newer information found (October 2026). No 2022-2026 register, vetting scheme or bill was found (English searches). ECPAT International Global Monitoring Report, The Gambia (2nd ed., c. 2015), recommendations: 'Establish effective mechanisms to monitor the movement of child sex offenders such as through the establishment of a child sex offender registry'; same in the executive summary (https://ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Ex_Summary_The-Gambia_FINAL.pdf, p. 7). Absence is inferred from the recommendation and is dated; no later registry found in: SORN 2022, ICMEC 2014, State Dept TIP 2025/2024 and HRR 2023 Gambia pages, UN Women VAW database, IHRDA SGBV handbook, and searches 'Gambia sex offenders register Children's Act' / 'Gambia "sex offender" register OR registry ... Sexual Offences Act 2013'. UK police FOI pages show only UK-registered offenders living in The Gambia.

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: Still none, by a newer source. Africanews (12 Apr 2024, citing BBC Amharic) said a register 'is reportedly in the works' at the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs, 'set to start operations next year', would bar offenders from schools and orphanages and may have a public page. No report that it started was found. SMART/Library of Congress, 'SORN Laws around the World' (2022; info cutoff Oct 2021), Appendix 'Notable countries currently without sex offender registries', p. 194 (PDF p. 205). No operating register verified.

Egypt

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: A bill is pending. The April 2026 bill by MP Amira El-Adly to add a national register of child sex offenders to the Penal Code ('سجل وطني للمعتدين جنسيًا على الأطفال') was referred to House committees. No report that it passed was found by October 2026. El Watan, 25 Apr 2026: a bill by MP Amira El-Adly amending Penal Code 58/1937 was referred to House committees; it would 'استحداث مادة جديدة تنص على إنشاء سجل وطني للمعتدين جنسيًا على الأطفال' (add a new article creating a national register of child sex offenders, with final convictions recorded and a ban on work with children), described as filling 'أحد أبرز أوجه القصور في المنظومة الحالية'. Absence is inferred from the bill creating a new register; adoption not verified. Also checked: SORN 2022 and ICMEC 2014 (no mention), State Dept TIP 2025/2024 and HRR 2023 Egypt pages (no registry mention), UN Women VAW database (no register measure); searches 'مصر سجل للمتحرشين والمعتدين جنسيا على الأطفال...' (ar) and 'Egypt sex offender registry proposal parliament harassers database' (en). ECPAT GMR Egypt (https://ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Global_Monitoring_Report-EGYPT.pdf) has no register mention.

Djibouti

No registry found, and no source saying there is none. Searched in October 2026 in English and the country's own languages; it is not in the US Justice Department's 2022 world survey or its 2014 overview.

What was searched (28 searches)
  • SORN Laws around the World (FRD/LoC for SMART, Apr 2022) https://smart.ojp.gov/doc/SORN-Laws-Around-the-World_FINAL_REPORT.pdf: full-text search of all 225 pages for 'Djibouti' - no entry in main report (41 countries) or appendix 'Notable countries currently without sex offender registries' (pp. 194-213); country not mentioned anywhere
  • Global Overview of Sex Offender Registration and Notification Systems https://www.icmec.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/US-Global-Overview-of-Sex-Offender-Systems.pdf (file at this URL is dated April 2014, 26 pp.): country not mentioned
  • US State Dept country pages grepped for 'sex offender|offender regist|register of|registry of|blacklist|black list|sexual predator|sex tourism': https://www.state.gov/reports/2025-trafficking-in-persons-report/djibouti/ , https://www.state.gov/reports/2024-trafficking-in-persons-report/djibouti/ , https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/djibouti/ - no registry mention
  • UN Women Global Database on Violence against Women, all measures listed for Djibouti (https://data.unwomen.org/global-database-on-violence-against-women/country-profile/Djibouti/measures): no sex offender register or vetting measure
  • WebSearch (fr): 'Djibouti registre délinquants sexuels fichier pédophiles enfants' - case news (dawan.africa) and old TIP reports only
  • WebSearch (en, combined): '"sex offender registry" ... "Djibouti"' - nothing country-specific
  • Round 2 WebSearch (fr): 'Djibouti fichier national délinquants sexuels protection de l'enfance loi registre' - old TIP reports, UNICEF, a birth-registration job ad
  • Round 2 WebSearch (ar): 'جيبوتي سجل مرتكبي الجرائم الجنسية ضد الأطفال' - unrelated cases in other countries
  • ECPAT pass (Oct 2026): ecpat.org country page https://ecpat.org/country/djibouti/ checked for linked resources and the ecpat.org WordPress search API queried for 'legal checklist' - no Legal Checklist published for this country (checklists found only for e.g. Côte d'Ivoire, DR Congo, Nepal, Ecuador). Disrupting Harm (ECPAT/INTERPOL/UNICEF) does not cover this country: phase 1 = 13 countries in Eastern/Southern Africa and South-East Asia, phase 2 = Armenia, Brazil, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Jordan, Mexico, Montenegro, Morocco, North Macedonia, Pakistan, Serbia, Tunisia (https://www.interpol.int/en/Crimes/Crimes-against-children/Projects/Disrupting-Harm2).
  • CRC concluding observations for DJI (documents.un.org, symbols CO: 2,3-5) full text searched for register/registry/database/vetting/screening/criminal record/sex offender/working with children - no recommendation to establish a sex offender register and no mention of one
  • Probed documents.un.org for CRC/C/OPSC/<ISO3>/CO/1 and /2 - none returned for this country
  • Code pénal de Djibouti (Equipo Nizkor copy, https://www.derechos.org/intlaw/doc/dji1.html) searched for fichier/registre/interdiction d'exercer/contact avec mineurs - only general penalties of 'interdiction d'exercer une activité professionnelle ou sociale'; no register
  • WebSearch (fr): 'Djibouti code pénal texte intégral pdf "atteintes sexuelles" mineurs peines complémentaires'
  • WebSearch (en): 'acerwc.africa concluding observations recommendations "sex offenders" register' and (fr) 'acerwc.africa observations finales Gabon OR Congo OR Djibouti OR Mali OR Guinée-Bissau OR Guinée équatoriale pdf' - no ACERWC concluding observation on a sex offender register found
  • WebSearch (fr): 'Djibouti recrutement enseignants dossier "casier judiciaire" ministère éducation nationale MENFOP' - only africarrieres.com general civil-service guide ('Ne pas avoir d'antécédents judiciaires incompatibles avec l'exercice de fonctions publiques'), not child-specific; not recorded
  • Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Impact / Childlight etc., https://outoftheshadows.global/en, linked from https://ispcan.org/global-reports/2026-out-of-the-shadows-index/): the site's country list has 60 countries and this country is not among them (country-page URL probes returned 404), so there is no indicator 2.3 'Background checks' or registry score for it
  • --- pass G (17 Oct 2026, new routes) ---
  • UN Universal Periodic Review documents, all cycles, downloaded by symbol from documents.un.org (https://documents.un.org/api/symbol/access?s=<symbol>&l=en&t=pdf; symbols found by probing A/HRC/WG.6/1-52/DJI/1-3) - national reports (/1), UN compilations (/2) and stakeholder summaries (/3): A/HRC/WG.6/16/DJI/1, A/HRC/WG.6/16/DJI/2, A/HRC/WG.6/16/DJI/3, A/HRC/WG.6/30/DJI/1, A/HRC/WG.6/30/DJI/2, A/HRC/WG.6/30/DJI/3, A/HRC/WG.6/44/DJI/1, A/HRC/WG.6/44/DJI/2, A/HRC/WG.6/44/DJI/3, A/HRC/WG.6/4/DJI/1, A/HRC/WG.6/4/DJI/2, A/HRC/WG.6/4/DJI/3. Result: no sex offender register, no recommendation to create one, no child-work vetting rule.
  • UN treaty-body documents listed on the OHCHR treaty body country page (https://tbinternet.ohchr.org/_layouts/15/TreatyBodyExternal/Countries.aspx?CountryCode=DJI&Lang=EN) downloaded from documents.un.org - CEDAW, Human Rights Committee (CCPR), CAT, CRPD concluding observations and the CEDAW/CRC/OPSC State party reports: CAT/C/DJI/CO/1, CCPR/C/DJI/CO/1, CEDAW/C/DJI/1-3, CEDAW/C/DJI/4-5, CEDAW/C/DJI/CO/1-3, CEDAW/C/DJI/CO/4-5, CRC/C/DJI/2, CRC/C/DJI/3-5. Same full-text search; no register or vetting scheme.
  • Older US State Department Country Reports on Human Rights Practices (2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 editions: https://www.state.gov/reports/<year>-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/djibouti/) and Trafficking in Persons Report country narratives (2018, 2020-2024 editions; the 2019 URL returned 404: https://www.state.gov/reports/<year>-trafficking-in-persons-report/djibouti/) full text searched for sex offender / offender regist / registry of / blacklist / background check / vetting / criminal record / pedophile - no mention of a sex offender register or child-work vetting.
  • ECPAT International media library listed through the WordPress API (https://ecpat.org/wp-json/wp/v2/media?mime_type=application/pdf, all pages, 601 PDFs) and searched by country name - no ECPAT Global Monitoring Report (2nd ed., 2011-2014) or A4A country monitoring report exists for this country.
  • WebSearch (fr): teacher-statute / private-school criminal-record searches: 'Burundi statut du personnel enseignant "casier judiciaire" recrutement enseignant loi', 'Tchad enseignement privé autorisation d'ouverture école "casier judiciaire" enseignants décret' (tchadinfos 4 Apr 2023 on the private-school compliance arrêté: no casier requirement mentioned), 'Congo Brazzaville enseignement privé loi "extrait de casier judiciaire" fondateur enseignants école', '"statut particulier" personnel enseignant Gabon "casier judiciaire" décret', 'Djibouti loi statut personnel enseignant "casier judiciaire" recrutement', 'Centrafrique statut particulier des enseignants "casier judiciaire" OR "bonne moralité" décret' - no teacher-specific criminal-record requirement found (results were Algerian, Belgian, Swiss, French)
  • WebSearch (fr): '"il n'existe pas de fichier" OR "absence de fichier" délinquants sexuels Gabon OR Congo OR Tchad OR Centrafrique OR Djibouti OR Comores OR Guinée OR Burundi' - no statement found
  • English Wikipedia 'Sex offender registry' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender_registry) read via WebFetch - country not mentioned (Wikipedia API returned HTTP 429 and the French FIJAIS article fetch was blocked, so other language editions could not be checked)
  • Read Djibouti's initial report to the ACERWC (French, https://www.acerwc.africa/sites/default/files/2022-09/Initial%20report%20Djibouti%20Fr.pdf) for casier/fichier/registre/moralité/antécédents/agrément/crèche/garderie - only Code de la famille art. 85 (guardian of a foundling must be of good morality); no criminal-record check or register
  • ecoi.net national-laws page for the country (https://www.ecoi.net/en/countries/<country>/national-laws) checked for penal, child-protection, education or GBV laws - only refugee, nationality, civil-status, constitution and asylum texts listed (no relevant law to read)
  • ACERWC member-state pages (https://www.acerwc.africa/en/member-states/<country>) returned 404; WebSearch (en) 'acerwc.africa concluding observations Burundi OR Chad OR Gabon OR Eritrea OR Djibouti OR Comoros "concluding observations" pdf' led to ACERWC reports to the AU Executive Council (July 2016, July 2017, February 2022: https://reporting.acerwc.africa/sites/default/files/2022-10/ACERWC%20Report%20to%20the%20Executive%20Council%20July%202016.pdf , https://www.acerwc.africa/sites/default/files/2022-10/ACERWC%20Report%20to%20the%20Executive%20Council%20July%202017.pdf , https://www.acerwc.africa/sites/default/files/2022-10/ACERWC%20Report%20to%20the%20Executive%20Council%20February%202022.pdf), full text searched for sex offender/register/registry/fichier/background check/vetting/criminal record/casier - nothing
  • WebSearch (fr): 'Djibouti nouveau code pénal 2024 OR 2025 "fichier" OR "registre" délinquants sexuels mineurs Assemblée nationale' - EEAS note on a retreat on reforming Djibouti's penal and criminal-procedure codes (https://www.eeas.europa.eu/node/430223_en); no register

No registry running, a source says: Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Enterprise/Economist Impact for Together for Girls, with Childlight; data collected in 2025), indicator 2.3 'Background checks' ('Does the country have strict criminal background check requirements for individuals working in direct contact with children?', rated 0-2; sources ECPAT International and Economist Impact research). Global data 2026 xlsx (https://assets.outoftheshadows.global/production/files/Global-data_2026.xlsx), sheet 'DATA TABLE' row 2.3: score 0; sheet 'Data_summary' row 2C: "Cameroon's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children." Score 0 is defined on https://outoftheshadows.global/en/indicators/background-checks as: 'National legislation does not include provisions requiring criminal background checks for people working with children and adolescents. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving direct contact with children.' The index has no separate sex-offender-registry indicator (registry maintenance is mentioned only as a budget item under 2.3). Country page: https://outoftheshadows.global/en/countries/cameroon. The index addresses background checks and bans, not registries directly; absence of a registry is inferred. Earlier searches for this country are in registries_final_A.json and the pass D not_found log (superseded). Also: not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016; no CRC concluding observation recommends a register.

Burkina Faso

No registry running, a source says: Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Enterprise/Economist Impact for Together for Girls, with Childlight; data collected in 2025), indicator 2.3 'Background checks' ('Does the country have strict criminal background check requirements for individuals working in direct contact with children?', rated 0-2; sources ECPAT International and Economist Impact research). Global data 2026 xlsx (https://assets.outoftheshadows.global/production/files/Global-data_2026.xlsx), sheet 'DATA TABLE' row 2.3: score 0; sheet 'Data_summary' row 2C: "Burkina Faso's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children." Score 0 is defined on https://outoftheshadows.global/en/indicators/background-checks as: 'National legislation does not include provisions requiring criminal background checks for people working with children and adolescents. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving direct contact with children.' The index has no separate sex-offender-registry indicator (registry maintenance is mentioned only as a budget item under 2.3). Country page: https://outoftheshadows.global/en/countries/burkina-faso. The index addresses background checks and bans, not registries directly; absence of a registry is inferred. Caveat: Code pénal 2018 Art. 219-13 refers to a penalty banning activity with habitual contact with minors in its rehabilitation rules only, with no article creating it. Earlier searches for this country are in registries_final_A.json and the pass D not_found log (superseded). Also: not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016; no CRC concluding observation recommends a register.

a233ff517fd8915c.h:
Bhutan

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: Still none, by a newer source. The Bhutanese (1 Aug 2022) reported that the Royal Bhutan Police 'has started work in setting up a Sex Offenders Registry' (a police-only online record shared with all stations), meaning none existed then. No later report that it is operating was found. SMART/Library of Congress, 'SORN Laws around the World' (2022; info cutoff Oct 2021), Appendix 'Notable countries currently without sex offender registries', p. 207 (PDF p. 218). Status 'No': no public registry as of 2021; 2019 call by a child-court bench member.

Nothing newer than the May 2024 calls for a paedophile registry during the Child Protection Bill debate was found. A June 2026 CBC report on 'offender monitoring' concerns electronic monitoring of people on bail, not a registry. CBC Barbados, 19 May 2024: 'Calls for the creation of a national registry of paedophiles' made by Youth Minister Charles Griffith during debate on the Child Protection Bill, backed by PM Mia Mottley and the National Committee on the Rights of the Child. Absence is inferred from these calls; no later enactment found. Also checked SORN 2022, ICMEC 2014, State Dept TIP/HRR pages, UN Women VAW database (only 'Rehabilitation of sexual offenders').

989d507cd4cc25ff.h:
Bahrain

No registry running, a source says: The 2022 US survey covers this country in one sentence about the whole region (no country there had registry laws), not in its own entry. SORN Laws around the World (Library of Congress Federal Research Division for DOJ SMART, Apr 2022), section 4.4 'Near East (North Africa and Middle East)', printed p. 141: '[Researchers determined that no countries within this region had laws pertaining to SORs.]' The regional appendix (printed pp. 205-206) lists only Israel, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. This is a region-wide statement, not a country-specific one, and reflects research up to 2021-2022; the same statement was used for Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon and Libya in registries_final_B.json. Bahrain-specific: Law No. 4 of 2021 (Restorative Justice Law for Children) Art. 39 creates only a confidential register of child-maltreatment cases at the Child Protection Centre (https://lloc.gov.bh/Legislation/HTM/K0421), not an offender register. CRC/C/BHR/CO/4-6 (27 Feb 2019, para. 29(d)) recommends 'a national database for all cases of violence against children' - a case database, not a sex offender register; CRC/C/OPSC/BHR/CO/1 and state report CRC/C/BHR/4-6 read: no offender register.

5938050d969448c0.h:
Armenia

No registry running, a source says: Re-checked October 2026: Still none, by a newer source. Armenia's reply to the Council of Europe (Lanzarote Committee) screening questionnaire, received 19 June 2026, describes no dedicated register and says there is 'no overarching legal requirement mandating systematic screening specifically for convictions for sexual offences'. Only sector rules exist, e.g. people with unexpunged convictions cannot compete for teaching posts, and foster/adoptive parents must show a police certificate. EVN Report, 22 Jun 2020: child-rights advocate Eduard Israelyan says pre-employment checks for crimes against children are not required ('Our legislation does not demand this'); a state database of offenders was only proposed after Lanzarote Convention ratification. Later status not verified (weak source).

No registry running, a source says: Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Enterprise/Economist Impact for Together for Girls, with Childlight; data collected in 2025), indicator 2.3 'Background checks' ('Does the country have strict criminal background check requirements for individuals working in direct contact with children?', rated 0-2; sources ECPAT International and Economist Impact research). Global data 2026 xlsx (https://assets.outoftheshadows.global/production/files/Global-data_2026.xlsx), sheet 'DATA TABLE' row 2.3: score 0; sheet 'Data_summary' row 2C: "Angola's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children." Score 0 is defined on https://outoftheshadows.global/en/indicators/background-checks as: 'National legislation does not include provisions requiring criminal background checks for people working with children and adolescents. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving direct contact with children.' The index has no separate sex-offender-registry indicator (registry maintenance is mentioned only as a budget item under 2.3). Country page: https://outoftheshadows.global/en/countries/angola. The index addresses background checks and bans, not registries directly; absence of a registry is inferred. Caveat: Decreto 46/06 Art. 7 (lex.ao) requires a criminal-record certificate from individual owners licensing for-profit creches/children's homes - owner licensing, not staff vetting, so not inconsistent with score 0. Earlier searches for this country are in registries_final_A.json and the pass D not_found log (superseded). Also: not in SORN 2022 or SMART/ICMEC 2014/2016; no CRC concluding observation recommends a register.

No registry running, a source says: The 2022 US survey covers this country in one sentence about the whole region (no country there had registry laws), not in its own entry. SORN Laws around the World (Library of Congress Federal Research Division for DOJ SMART, Apr 2022), section 4.4 'Near East (North Africa and Middle East)', printed p. 141: '[Researchers determined that no countries within this region had laws pertaining to SORs.]' The regional appendix (printed pp. 205-206) lists only Israel, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. This is a region-wide statement, not a country-specific one, and reflects research up to 2021-2022; the same statement was used for Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon and Libya in registries_final_B.json. Algeria-specific: Algérie360 (30 Sep 2013, https://www.algerie360.com/letat-determine-a-assurer-une-meilleure-protection-juridique-a-lenfance/) reported a national petition asking for 'la mise en place d'un fichier national des pédophiles dans les dossiers de police', implying none then. CRC concluding observations CRC/C/DZA/CO/3-4 (2012) read: no register recommendation or mention. No later register found.

A Labour Code reform (Draft Law No. 218/2026) would bar people convicted of offences against children from jobs with regular contact with children and require a detailed criminal-record certificate that also shows expunged convictions. Parliament passed it in first reading on 2 July and, per Moldova's Council of Europe reply, in second reading on 30 July 2026, but it was not yet published, so not in force; it is a vetting rule, not a register. A source says no sex-offender registry is running here (or only a planned one)

Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Impact / Together for Girls), indicator 2.3 'Background checks', Data_summary sheet of the official workbook: 'Mongolia's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children.' This states that no child-work vetting scheme or conviction-based bar exists in national law; it does not separately address a police-only offender register. Other findings this pass: the 2016 Law on Child Protection (legalinfo.mn/mn/detail/11710), art. 18.1.8, told the central child-protection agency to 'build a database, together with law enforcement, on citizens and legal entities who committed crimes or violations against children, children in conflict with the law, and witness and victim children' and use it in its work. That law was replaced by the revised Law on Child Protection of 17 Jan 2024. The Ministry's final draft of the revision (mlsp.gov.mn/uploads/files/khuukhed_khamgaalal_law_draft_final_last.pdf) no longer has this perpetrator database. It keeps only a database of at-risk children and services (art. 2.3, item 2.10) and a bar on appointing persons convicted of crimes against children as guardians (art. 4.10.1.4). The enacted 2024 text could not be retrieved: legalinfo.mn search is script-driven. No implementation of the 2016 database was found. CRC documents checked: CRC/C/MNG/CO/3-4 and CO/5, CRC/C/OPSC/MNG/CO/1 (3 Mar 2010), state reports and lists of issues. None mentions a register.

3f93423725bb37b8.h:
Timor-Leste

A source says no sex-offender registry is running here (or only a planned one)

Para. 24: 'the Committee urges the State Party to: ... (d) Ensure the effective implementation of the Primero software platform for child protection case management and the establishment of a sexual offenders registration system'. A recommendation to establish such a system means none is in place as of Sep 2026. The State party's replies to the list of issues (CRC/C/TLS/RQ/4) describe only the Primero CPIMS+ case-management tool (launched 2024 by the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion), not an offender register. Earlier passes: no entry in SORN Laws around the World 2022 or the SMART/ICMEC 2016 overview.

e8e8d4645095acfc.h:
Venezuela

A source says no sex-offender registry is running here (or only a planned one)

Out of the Shadows Index 2026 (Economist Impact / Together for Girls), indicator 2.3 'Background checks', Data_summary sheet of the official workbook: 'Venezuela's national legislation does not include provisions which mandate or include non-mandatory provisions for criminal background checks. Convicted sex offenders are not prohibited from holding positions involving or facilitating direct contact with children.' This states that no child-work vetting scheme or conviction-based bar exists in national law; it does not separately address a police-only offender register. Also read this pass: the Ley para la Prevención y Erradicación del Abuso Sexual contra Niñas, Niños y Adolescentes (Gaceta Oficial 6.655 Ext., 7 Oct 2021; text at https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-05/6-prevencionabusosexual_digital_v1.pdf). It sets up no register. Its only conviction consequence is loss of parental authority (art. 19). The 2021 reform of the Ley Orgánica sobre el Derecho de las Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia (Gaceta 6.667 Ext., 16 Dec 2021) creates only a 'registro único de denuncias', a register of complaints, not of offenders. CRC documents checked: CRC/C/VEN/CO/2, CO/3-5, CRC/C/OPSC/VEN/CO/1 (3 Nov 2014). No register mentioned.
